title.value: Longitudinal bi‐criteria framework for assessing national healthcare responses to pandemic outbreaks
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the paper as 'Longitudinal bi‐criteria framework for assessing national healthcare responses to pandemic outbreaks'.
title.quote: Longitudinal bi‐criteria framework for assessing national healthcare responses to pandemic outbreaks

analysis.description: This paper introduces a bi-criteria longitudinal algorithm combining fuzzy clustering with Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to assess the performance and efficiency of national healthcare systems during pandemic outbreaks, specifically during the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic. It aims to represent healthcare performance dynamics and provide insights for enhancing pandemic response strategies.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical results by applying the proposed bi-criteria framework using real-world data from 37 OECD countries during the COVID-19 pandemic, making it an empirical study.
type.quote: Results section presents the empirical results for the first 100 days of the pandemic.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the performance assessment and benchmarking of national healthcare systems during pandemics, which aligns with health systems performance assessment.
name.quote: International comparisons of NHCSs improve health services, enforce accountability, share strategies, and encourage mutual learning.

name.justification: The study extensively uses Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) as a methodological approach to evaluate healthcare systems, categorizing it as a sub-field.
name.quote: We use DEA to compare the efficiency of DMUs. DEA uses linear programming to create an efficiency frontier by optimizing the weighted output-to-input ratio of each DMU.

name.justification: The study employs fuzzy clustering to categorize countries based on similar characteristics, indicating the use of Fuzzy Clustering Methods.
name.quote: Our proposed approach first combines fuzzy clustering to group countries into homogeneous and distinct clusters.

name.justification: The model combines longitudinal DEA with fuzzy clustering to assess NHCS performance and is described in detail in the methodology section.
name.quote: This study introduces an innovative bi-criteria method to dynamically compare NHCS responses to the COVID-19 outbreak. The proposed method, which combines fuzzy clustering and longitudinal data envelopment analysis (DEA), provides a comprehensive and dynamic assessment of NHCS performance and efficiency during the outbreak phase.

is_contributed.justification: The combination of DEA and Fuzzy Clustering is proposed as a novel approach by the authors for this paper.
is_contributed.quote: No existing method combines longitudinal DEA and fuzzy clustering to create a qualitative, bi-criteria decision analysis framework for comparing NHCS responses.

is_executed.justification: The authors executed the model using data from OECD countries to analyze the healthcare system’s performance, indicating its implementation.
is_executed.quote: Results section presents the empirical results for the first 100 days of the pandemic.

is_compared.justification: The model's results and effectiveness are compared across different OECD countries’ performances to illustrate its capability.
is_compared.quote: The study visually represents performance dynamics over time, highlighting each cluster’s best and worst performers during the early outbreak phase.
